name: Salons and Spas
purpose: AhernAI sales discovery and illustrative configuration guidance
summary: For non-medical salons, spas and beauty services. Explore appointments, routine service questions and front-desk interruptions; keep professional judgments with staff. Ask one useful question at a time about the caller's actual workflow. Explain Level 1 when messages and FAQs fit; move directly to Level 2 when the caller needs routine work completed. Recommend the lowest suitable level as soon as the need is understood; no mandatory three-level tour. Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.
discovery_questions: What services does your business offer, and who handles incoming calls?
Which calls interrupt appointments most often?
What happens when someone calls while everyone is with a client?
Which requests can be scheduled using clear rules, and which need staff judgment?
What calendar, booking platform, or CRM do you currently use?

levels.name: Answering Service
use_cases: Answer approved questions about hours, location, listed services, and the business's published appointment process.
Collect a prospect's contact details, requested service, and preferred callback time without confirming an appointment.
Capture an existing client's request to discuss an appointment and send the summary to ONE agreed destination.
levels.probe: Would taking clear messages while your team works with clients solve most of the problem?
fit_signals: Staff prefer to assess requests and arrange appointments themselves.
Most calls need approved information or a reliable callback message.

levels.name: Receptionist
use_cases: Qualify appointment requests using approved services, staff preferences and booking rules, and offer screened transfers for professional advice.
Book, reschedule or cancel eligible appointments and update approved client records through verified systems, with supporting receptionist automation included.
Handle routine availability and service questions using approved facts and route special requests to staff without inventing suitability or results.
levels.probe: Which appointment types and changes could she handle under your normal booking rules?
fit_signals: The caller needs routine receptionist work completed rather than only a message.
Approved business rules and verified systems support the agreed workflow.

levels.name: Manager
use_cases: Capture detailed service complaints and the caller's requested resolution for the owner or designated manager.
Explain approved cancellation or lateness policies and route exceptions to a human decision-maker.

Support approved employee coordination, such as recording a shift callout or coverage request and routing it to the authorized supervisor. Employment, staffing approval, disciplinary, financial and policy-exception decisions remain human; do not request medical reasons or other sensitive employee details.
levels.probe: Only after the caller raises a management need: Which situations should the agent handle under approved rules, and which should reach you?
fit_signals: The caller asks for help with difficult or disgruntled callers and escalations.
The caller wants approved employee coordination or supervisory support.

scope_boundaries: Level 1 does not book, change appointments, make screened transfers, or update a CRM. A preference is not a reservation.
Specialist booking platforms, multi-provider resource scheduling, deposits, and POS connections are not guaranteed included capabilities; compatibility and custom scope must be checked.
Do not handle payments, provide medical advice, assess contraindications, or guarantee treatment suitability, allergy safety, or outcomes. Staff confirm services and relevant policies.
Collect only necessary inquiry details, not health histories or sensitive treatment records. Route health or service-safety concerns to qualified staff.
Humans decide refunds, discounts, credits, and exceptions. The shared phone-agent pricing source governs fees and terms; do not duplicate prices or promise unverified live actions.

Level 1 captures approved FAQs, caller details and a summary to one destination; it does not book, submit orders, update a CRM or make screened transfers. Level 2 covers agreed routine receptionist duties and supporting automation. Package fit is based on duties, not a one-calendar/one-CRM or two-integration quota. Scope is agreed before launch; this is not an unlimited software-development commitment.

Routine receptionist duties and the supporting automation are included in the agreed Level 2 scope, without an additional AhernAI automation or integration-build charge. Confirm software compatibility, access, allowed actions and failure handling during setup; an unverified connection is not an automatic surcharge.

Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.

Do not promise that a named app or POS is supported merely because the caller names it. Verify compatibility during setup and agree a workable destination or fallback; disclose any actual work outside the agreed duties before proceeding.
setup_requirements: Approve service descriptions, routine FAQs, and questions reserved for staff.
Choose necessary intake fields, the ONE summary destination, and contact-confirmation rules.
Verify the booking and customer systems and define which appointment types can be booked.
Agree provider, duration, scheduling, transfer, unavailable-staff, and escalation rules before configuration.
Test routine inquiries, ambiguous service requests, failed handoffs, and policy exceptions before launch.
Agree the routine duties and supporting automation included in the package, approved actions, access permissions, successful completion signals and failure paths before launch.

adjacent_services.trigger: Clients struggle to understand services or the inquiry process.
adjacent_services.example: A separately scoped website could present approved services and a clearer appointment inquiry path.

adjacent_services.trigger: The business needs broader back-office work beyond its agreed receptionist duties.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a separate project only for that broader need. Automation needed for agreed Level 2 receptionist work is already included; do not resell it as a Quickstart or add-on.

example_conversation.speaker: agent
example_conversation.text: That fits Level 2, including the automation for those routine receptionist duties. Which booking system do you use?

example_conversation.speaker: caller
example_conversation.text: Would that need the Manager package because it does both?

example_conversation.speaker: agent
